customer_acme_ops: Hey — we're seeing intermittent 500s and spikes in latency from a few of our services around 2026-02-11 11:02–11:10 UTC. We don't have a clear request id yet, can you tell us what to grab?

maria_support: Sorry about that — we can definitely help. The quickest thing that helps us correlate traces is a Request ID / Trace ID from the response or the Console. Few quick asks: 1) send one full request id (exact string), 2) the approximate UTC timestamp window, 3) SDK version and region, 4) if possible attach a HAR or curl output.

customer_acme_ops: OK. Where do I find the request id in the SDK and in the Console?

maria_support: Short answers:
- REST/HTTP: look for the response header `x-request-id` (server-generated) or SDK-provided `request_id`/`meta.request_id`.
- Node/Python SDKs typically expose it on the response object.
- Console: Redwood Console -> Requests (or Model -> Requests) -> find the timestamp and copy the Request ID.

maria_support: Node example to log header / meta:
```js
const res = await client.responses.create({ input: '...' });
console.log(res.headers && res.headers['x-request-id']); // raw header when present
console.log(res.request_id || res.meta?.request_id); // SDK helpers
```

maria_support: Python example:
```py
resp = client.responses.create(input='...')
print(resp.request_id or resp.meta.get('request_id') or resp.headers.get('x-request-id'))
```

dev_jules: For curl, capture headers so you can see x-request-id: use `-D -` to dump headers. Example repro that prints headers and body:
```bash
curl -D - -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/responses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```
Look for `x-request-id:` in the response headers. Copy that exact string into this thread.

customer_acme_ops: We use streaming in one service. Does the request id still show up?

maria_support: Yes — for streaming endpoints the request id is included in the initial response headers before the stream body. If you're using an SSE/websocket client, it will often appear in the connection/open event metadata. If you only see chunks, try to capture the initial connection headers (curl / `-i`) or enable debug logging in the SDK to print connection metadata.

eng_tomas: If you can't get the x-request-id from the client, we can still find traces if you give us: account/org id, exact minute window (prefer 30s–2m window), model name, and any snippet of the prompt. We search logs by timestamp & model and then correlate.

maria_support: For the Console: top-right -> Requests -> filter by project/customer -> use the timestamp at the top to narrow down. Click the row to expand details and copy the request id (looks like a hex or UUID). If you want a permalink, click “Copy Request Link” and paste it here.

customer_acme_ops: Any privacy concerns — do we redact anything?

maria_support: Yes please: remove full API keys and any PII from prompts. Helpful to include last 4 digits of API key (we'll ask) and the SDK version. For HAR/debug bundles: sanitize user tokens and personal data, we only need request/response metadata and headers (x-request-id, status codes), and the request body for repro (with PII removed).

maria_support: Debug bundle checklist we typically ask for:
- One example request id (from response header)
- Exact UTC timestamp window (eg 2026-02-11T11:03:42Z ± 60s)
- SDK + language + SDK version (eg node 2.4.1)
- Model name and region (eg redwood-1, us-west1)
- A curl reproduction (or HAR file) with `-D -` so headers are visible
- Any console/SDK logs around the time (set LOG_LEVEL=debug if safe)
- App environment (prod/staging), and whether requests passed through proxy/ingress

dev_jules: Example curl that both reproduces and shows headers, and also includes how to include a client-side correlation id if you want to force one for testing:
```bash
# reproduce and show headers
curl -D - -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/responses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"repro prompt"}'
# optionally send your own correlation id (helps correlate client/server logs):
curl -D - -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/responses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: my-local-test-123" \
  -d '{"input":"repro prompt"}'
```
Sending `X-Request-ID` can be useful for local reproduction but note the server will still return its canonical x-request-id header; share either value.

customer_acme_ops: Got it. Here's a sample from one of our runs (we redacted prompts):
- Time window: 2026-02-11T11:04:10Z -> 2026-02-11T11:04:20Z
- curl headers from response: HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
  x-request-id: 0af4e3b2-9f1a-4d3c-8d2f-3b6a9a8e7c2f
  content-type: application/json
- SDK: node 2.4.1, region us-west1

maria_support: Perfect — that's exactly what we need. We'll escalate to infra with that request id. Eng will ping once we locate the trace.

ops_bot: Incident created: INC-20260211-4321 assigned to eng_tomas. Related request id 0af4e3b2-9f1a-4d3c-8d2f-3b6a9a8e7c2f.

eng_tomas: Thanks — I have the request id. Quick follow-up: can you also attach a HAR or the full curl output (body + headers) for that request id? If you can't, send the raw request payload and a screenshot of the Console entry.

customer_acme_ops: Will upload the HAR to the secure link in DM. Thanks for the quick help.

maria_support: Thanks — once we have the HAR + request id we'll post back with findings or ask for more logs. :thumbsup:
